status: Selected planning list; not purchased, assembled or acoustically qualified
user_decision: Howard selected the M50 for now and requested the final equipment list.
scope: Sound playback and acoustic measurement on the existing Mac; neural hardware integration is deferred.

target.adaptation: 96 kSa/s is this Mac interface plan; the paper used 192 kSa/s. Digital sample arithmetic does not verify acoustic fidelity.
open_protocol_choices: The exact initial 37-frequency array is not supplied in the paper methods; do not reconstruct it as an exact published array.
Ramp shape is unspecified in the paper. Any chosen shape must be labeled a Rice choice.

Speaker distance, orientation, target level, level convention and numerical acceptance tolerances: TBD with Howard and the professor. The paper reports approximately 80 dB SPL at sheep-ear distance; this is a reference, not an approved Rice exposure setting.

parts.host_check: Prefer a direct Mac USB-C connection supplying at least 0.9 A at 5 V. Exact Mac/OS and host settings still require verification.
parts.routing_check: Set Monitor Mix fully to DAW and disable software input monitoring so recorded microphone sound is not fed back to the speaker.
parts.limits: Only one microphone/line input; the other input is an instrument input with a 20 kHz specified band. This is not a completed neural-recorder synchronization design. Working-gain response remains to be measured.

parts.evidence_scope: The official response illustration supports output near 32 kHz. Its geometry, drive level and uncertainty are unspecified, and it does not establish short-pip fidelity or the required SPL in our setup.
parts.settings: Use wired TRS, Monitor mode, documented EQ/room controls, fixed gains and recorded firmware/standby settings. Verify which input drives the selected cabinet.
parts.limits: Usable level, distortion, ringing and 10 ms sequence behavior at the reference position remain unmeasured. Upgrade only if the test identifies a limitation that another speaker addresses.

parts.fit_check: M50 ADP1 and half-inch calibrator port nominally match; check insertion and seal on receipt.

M50 -> HMIC-010 -> iD4 rear XLR microphone input, with 48 V phantom enabled
R8090 + included M50 ADP1 -> M50 for the 1 kHz level-reference check; remove the calibrator for free-field measurements

software_plan.status: Proposed; not installed, implemented or hardware-tested by this change
software_plan.candidate: Python with NumPy and python-sounddevice for waveform arrays and simultaneous playback/recording; analysis and serial calibration import to be implemented.
requirements: Select iD4 input/output explicitly and use native 96 kSa/s; document Mac Audio MIDI Setup and software settings.
Precompute one continuous sequence with 960 samples per 10 ms pip and ramps inside that duration. Do not schedule each pip with a 10 ms operating-system sleep.
Save the exact waveform, tone schedule, gain/geometry/settings and unprocessed microphone recording.
Apply the serial-specific frequency correction and fixed-gain level reference using a documented level convention.
Check stream status, clipping and missing samples/events; avoid Bluetooth and microphone-to-speaker monitoring feedback.

bench_acceptance_plan: Check the serial calibration file, connections, Mac USB power, native sample rate, selected cabinet and microphone-monitor routing before playback.
Record a background segment and document microphone/speaker distance, height, orientation and room conditions.
Establish/check the fixed-gain recording level with the R8090, including before/after repeatability. Keep microphone frequency correction separate from this 1 kHz level check.

Measure the required frequencies at the reference position, including the 32 kHz endpoint, at the intended level. Record response, clipping, distortion within the measurement band and headroom; do not equalize by demanding unavailable speaker output.

Record repeated continuous 10 ms sequences and inspect duration, onset spacing, frequency transitions, level consistency, ringing into the following pip and missing events. A single detected tone or a long sweep is not this test.

Measure/document acoustic delay and variability with a suitable electrical/acoustic reference when that timing claim is required. A fixed delay longer than 10 ms does not itself prevent a continuous 100-pip/s sequence.
Have Howard and the professor set numerical pass tolerances before judging the test. Retain MR3 only if the measured sequence meets those criteria.
measurement_limits: M50 and 96 kSa/s capture cannot quantify the 64 kHz second harmonic of a 32 kHz tone; do not claim complete ultrasonic THD coverage.
The iD4 plan does not establish TTL markers or alignment to a future neural recorder.
The sound-only plan does not qualify animal use. Rice sedation remains an adaptation from the paper's awake, alert sheep.
actions: Research and planning only. No order, vendor contact, software installation, sound playback, bench measurement or animal experiment occurred.
followup_note: Subsequent audit records the initial mouse checkout, independent sheep recalibration, unverified MR3 qualification and a proposed iD14/two-TRS-cable revision. This original $2005.91 iD4 parts snapshot is preserved.
